about: Guided paths through the site, one per kind of reader. Optional and light: a reader who ignores them sees the site as it is. Each stop answers one question the reader asks, in one line, with at most two sections to read first and one thing to do. Every path ends at Join. Read by tools/site-nav.js and tools/build-pages.js; the monthly update may refresh the lines, under the same tone checks.

end.why: Common Shade is a collaborative: shade is something we hold up together.

paths.label: Funders and philanthropy
paths.card: Where support could matter most, what works, and who could carry it to people.
paths.join: Bring a question, a portfolio or a place.

stops.q: Where is the need?
stops.why: Twelve cities and what heat is doing in each, with the plans already in place.

stops.q: What works, and how sure are we?
stops.why: 131 ways to protect people, each with its evidence, cost and limits.
do: Read the Lancet Countdown for funders

stops.q: What is still unknown?
stops.why: Twelve questions the evidence has not yet answered, each sized for one well-designed study, and where evidence looks stronger than the funding we traced.
do: See the gaps in the Lancet's evidence

stops.q: Where is money flowing, and where is it not?
stops.why: Fifty pieces of traced funding, followed from who gave them to the cycles they could help break, with the role each plays.
read: Cycles we have not yet traced

stops.q: Who could carry it to people?
stops.why: For each action, who could permit it, pay for it, deliver it and check it, with the organisations already at work and the parts where we found no one yet.

stops.q: How could a few grants work together?
stops.why: Choose Sketch a portfolio: a few grants across places and roles, and see which cycles it reaches, what it leans on and what would make it last.
do: Twenty-four questions to ask before a grant starts

paths.label: City and local government
paths.card: Your city’s heat, the actions that fit, and a plan your team can run.
paths.join: Share what your city is trying, and what you need.

stops.q: What is heat doing in our city?
stops.why: Twelve city profiles: the kind of heat, the plan in place and the cycles at work.

stops.q: What happens to our power, water and clinics?
stops.why: Stress-test a city’s systems through a five-day heatwave, and see which protection helps most.
do: See who holds each part up

stops.q: What can we do this season?
stops.why: Actions by setting, each with who acts and what keeps it working.

stops.q: How have other places done it?
stops.why: Plans from Ahmedabad, Thane, Tamil Nadu, Singapore and Dhaka.

stops.q: Which actions fit together here?
stops.why: Choose your place, add actions, and see what they could help interrupt, what each depends on and who acts.
do: Turn it into a six-step plan

stops.q: How do we turn this into a plan?
stops.why: Six steps, from who you protect to the alerts that switch actions on.

stops.q: How will we pay for it?
stops.why: What needs paying for, when money is needed, and what has been tried.

stops.q: How do clinics prepare?

stops.q: How do we plan the season?
stops.why: A workbook that checks your plan against WHO’s core elements.
